builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: When Disclosure Is Compulsory: Evaluating Ride-Hailing Rebalancing Policies with Self-Interested LLM Driver Agents
summary: The method replaces analytical or fully-compliant-driver simulation of ride-hailing rebalancing policies with a simulation of self-interested LLM driver agents reacting to disclosed platform rules. It costs the engineering effort of building a multi-agent simulation environment plus per-run API inference for each driver agent, and it introduces dependence on the chosen LLM's interpretation fidelity. What can fail is ecological validity: LLM agents may not reproduce real driver behavior, the two tested models may not generalize to other LLMs, and the simulation results are specific to the modeled zones and policies.
rationale: The technique is a research framework for evaluating regulatory and marketplace policy questions, not a production component an ML engineer with constrained infrastructure would deploy to serve users.
technique: LLM-Agent Simulation for Ride-Hailing Policy Evaluation

claims.statement: The method replaces analytical or fully-compliant-driver simulation of ride-hailing rebalancing policies with a simulation of self-interested LLM driver agents reacting to disclosed platform rules. It costs the engineering effort of building a multi-agent simulation environment plus per-run API inference for each driver agent, and it introduces dependence on the chosen LLM's interpretation fidelity. What can fail is ecological validity: LLM agents may not reproduce real driver behavior, the two tested models may not generalize to other LLMs, and the simulation results are specific to the modeled zones and policies.

Under mandatory rule disclosure, self-interested LLM driver agents reduce relocation-offer declines in Manhattan from ~80% to ~25%; reactive policy R loses 3.7% platform profit, anticipatory policy A is unchanged, and A becomes a win-win-win with driver income, platform profit, and service rate each rising 10-12%.
